churn_resistance.rationale: The data-access layer is a model of churn resistance — one module, typed end to end — but the previous-model segment config is copy-pasted across all seven route files, plus two small duplicated helpers, so a framework major upgrade ripples across the whole route tree.

findings.issue: The app is built on the 'previous model' caching API (`dynamic`/`revalidate`/`fetchCache` segment configs). Next 16.0 removes these when Cache Components is enabled, and the Next 16.4 blog (2026-10-06) recommends Cache Components for every app, making it the default in Next 17.
findings.suggestion: Adopt `cacheComponents` now: delete the segment configs (an official codemod exists), and let data fetching be dynamic by default with `use cache`/`cacheLife` for the long-lived list data — the app's always-fresh requirement maps cleanly onto it and gains the static shell/streaming benefits it currently gets none of.

findings.issue: `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` and `revalidate = 0` are repeated in five pages and the layout; the root layout's declarations already apply to child segments, and pages reading searchParams are dynamic anyway.
findings.suggestion: Declare it once in the root layout (or, better, nowhere once Cache Components makes dynamic the default) so the migration surface is one file instead of seven.

findings.issue: Raw for sprites and artwork (also app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:175) instead of next/image, the framework's recommended image primitive.
findings.suggestion: Use next/image with `unoptimized` (or a remotePattern built from API_BASE_URL) to stay on the recommended path while keeping the runtime-configured origin.

findings.issue: apiFetch has no AbortSignal or timeout, so a stalled upstream hangs the server render with no recovery path.
findings.suggestion: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` and clear the in-flight cache entry on abort, which the existing `promise.catch` cleanup already half-supports.

findings.issue: The `first()` query-param helper is duplicated verbatim in app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:25.
findings.suggestion: Move it next to the other query/serialization helpers in lib/format.ts.

findings.issue: A catch-all route re-renders the same content as root not-found.tsx solely to set the document title, and responds with HTTP 200.
findings.suggestion: Keep it, but call `notFound()` from the catch-all (or a not-found boundary) so the built-in 404 pipeline handles it and the status code is correct, setting the title via the root layout's metadata when possible.

findings.issue: The module-level Map cache never invalidates for the life of the process, so a long-running server serves first-fetch data forever despite the spec treating the API as live.
findings.suggestion: Add a TTL per entry, or move the shared lookups to `use cache` with a `cacheLife` profile once Cache Components is adopted.

findings.issue: idFromUrl extracts IDs with a regex on a URL string.
findings.suggestion: Parse with `new URL(url)` and read `pathname` segments — the platform primitive, and self-documenting.

summary: A lean, current-generation App Router app: Next 16.4.3, async request APIs, typed data access funnelled through a single lib/api.ts module, and zero runtime dependencies beyond next/react. The one real forward-looking gap is that it is built on the previous-model caching API (`dynamic`/`revalidate`/`fetchCache`) that Next 16.4 now recommends replacing and that becomes the default in Next 17 — and it is copy-pasted across all seven route files rather than declared once. Secondary items are raw instead of next/image and fetches without a timeout.

apis.api: Route segment config: dynamic / revalidate / fetchCache
apis.replacement: Cache Components (`cacheComponents: true`) with `use cache` / `cacheLife`; dynamic fetching is the default there. Source: nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config (v16.0.0 removes these when Cache Components is enabled) and nextjs.org/blog/next-16-4
Documented Next pattern for updating the URL without a server round-trip; Next syncs its router state with native history updates
Redundant since fetch is uncached by default in Next 15+, but harmless and explicit
next/image (with `unoptimized` or a remotePattern derived from API_BASE_URL); flagged by eslint-plugin-next no-img-element
